visitors.title: Archive Curator
visitors.subtitle: Central Canon Observatory
lines: The chronology is not decoration. Every gap marks an unresolved authority problem.
The Atlas earns its scale by refusing to fill silence with invention.
Meridian becomes legible only after the people inside it can no longer interrupt the composition.
thoughts: Every room here is an argument against amnesia.
He keeps turning memory into architecture because ordinary memory has failed him before.

visitors.title: Game Visitor
visitors.subtitle: West Gameworks
lines: This wing understands that place has mechanics. Duncan is not wallpaper.
The tiny town is convincing because the rules are local before the scenery is local.
Smudge collects scale itself, not merely clutter.
thoughts: Even the cat game is secretly urban phenomenology.
I expected whimsy. I did not expect systems theory.

visitors.title: Myth Systems Researcher
visitors.subtitle: West Systems Workshop
lines: He builds myth the way other people build databases, and somehow both remain true.
The control room is frightening because it records authority instead of flattering it.
The familiar is not a mascot. It is a visible state machine with opinions.
thoughts: No wonder the projects keep circling ethics, witness, and record.
The mythic scale is carrying extremely practical anxieties.

visitors.title: Local-first Engineer
visitors.subtitle: East Local Systems Lab
lines: The discipline is the point: local, inspectable, recoverable, and honest about failure states.
Relay Link does not pretend a dropped bridge is still connected. That is rarer than it should be.
DexDictate treats privacy as architecture, not a footer promise.
thoughts: He distrusts invisible systems, so he keeps making visible ones.
Every convenience here has to survive an audit.

visitors.title: Forensic Analyst
visitors.subtitle: East Local Systems Lab
lines: Even the investigative tools are shaped by consent, scope, provenance, and restraint.
The evidence trays are more important than the tool count.
A local model is useful here only if the chain of custody remains visible.
thoughts: The paranoia is moral architecture, not merely mood.
This person has been taught, repeatedly, that undocumented authority is dangerous.

visitors.title: Memory Architect
visitors.subtitle: East Local Systems Lab
lines: DexVault makes the underlying fear explicit: losing the thread is a form of damage.
The archive does not resolve contradictions just because retrieval found both of them.
A source-grounded answer is a path through rooms, not a sentence from nowhere.
thoughts: Of course the archive itself becomes sacred furniture.
The retrieval system is trying to make continuity less fragile than a human nervous system.

visitors.title: Accessibility Visitor
visitors.subtitle: Rear Sanctuary
lines: Dexter is sacred here, but not sentimentalized. Blindness changes the route, and the room honors that.
The scent markers are care translated into spatial design.
The dog is allowed to remain difficult, specific, and real.
thoughts: The tenderness is all in the structure, never in the performance.
This sanctuary understands that access changes the world rather than merely adding instructions.

visitors.title: Floor Docent
visitors.subtitle: Museum Staff
lines: Please notice that the installations change in place. Nothing is a slideshow pretending to be a room.
The museum is organized by governing problem, not by date.
You are allowed to disagree with the labels. The artifacts are the stronger evidence.
thoughts: A good tour should leave the visitor with sharper questions, not a flattened biography.
The building is finally beginning to behave like a building.

visitors.title: Gallery Attendant
visitors.subtitle: Museum Staff
lines: The central installations are interactive. The walls are not touchscreens.
Please keep the path clear around the floor-plan kiosk.
No, the dog does not speak. The room is still listening.
thoughts: I have stopped counting how many people try to pet Dexter’s figure.
At least this museum admits when a system is unavailable.

visitors.title: Installation Conservator
visitors.subtitle: Museum Staff
lines: The wall reliefs are intentionally fixed. Their orientation belongs to the building.
This installation has more moving state than most museums would permit.
Maintenance is part of the interpretation when failure states are the subject.
thoughts: I appreciate an artist who labels the dangerous assumptions.
The difficult part is preserving a system that is supposed to remain unfinished.

visitors.title: Design Student
visitors.subtitle: Visiting Pair
lines: The official-versus-actual switch is doing more narrative work than a whole cutscene.
Look at the ring: it is material, not symbolic anatomy.
The museum keeps refusing the easiest visual metaphor.
thoughts: I need to steal the method, not the aesthetics.
The constraints are making the images stranger and more exact.

visitors.title: Systems Student
visitors.subtitle: Visiting Pair
lines: The system is teaching canon through state transitions instead of a lore dump.
The six-month pacing is the exhibit. The station model is only the evidence.
The strongest interaction here is being forced to wait.
thoughts: This is a continuity database disguised as horror.
I did not expect the timing model to feel accusatory.

visitors.title: Seated Sketcher
visitors.subtitle: West Gameworks
lines: I am drawing the grade of the street, not the skyline. The grade is the mechanic.
The ferry is a clock that the player has to inhabit.
Rain should change the hand before it changes the color palette.
thoughts: The whole wing is a study of how geography disciplines bodies.
I should stop sketching the props and diagram the waiting.

visitors.title: Visiting Architect
visitors.subtitle: Threshold Hall
lines: The good choice was turning the introduction into a vestibule rather than a menu.
The portal frames make the canon wing feel earned.
This building finally behaves like a place that expects return visits.
thoughts: Now the museum has sequence, not just content.
The architecture is helping the biography stay oblique.

visitors.title: System Pilgrim
visitors.subtitle: Rear Sanctuary
lines: The sanctuary is convincing because it is specific: blindness, scent, route, rest.
The sacred part is not the glow. The sacred part is the accommodation.
Dexter is treated as a governing presence, not a mascot.
thoughts: Care is more believable when it changes the floor plan.
I trust rooms that have learned from a single animal.

visitors.title: Continuity Researcher
visitors.subtitle: Central Canon Observatory
lines: He keeps building systems that admit contradictions into the room.
The most interesting thing here is that the labels do not overpromise.
The museum reads like a self-portrait made of methodologies.
thoughts: This is autobiography disguised as infrastructure.
The projects rhyme through evidence discipline.

visitors.title: Media Researcher
visitors.subtitle: Central Canon Observatory
lines: The outreach film folio on the wall reframes the whole war section.
There is something refreshing about a museum that lets the artifact stay a little ugly.
The more specific the canon gets, the less decorative it feels.
thoughts: Texture arrives through rule-following here, not random detail.
I like that even the mock ephemera has a doctrine behind it.
